subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` calls permanently reject legacy ownerless session rows, leaving their management to operators and non-plugin clients?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but this changes the persisted authorization contract for existing installations and requires explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve strict ownership
options.body: Keep fail-closed denial, document the non-plugin recovery path, and require deployed proof before merge.

options.title: Require migration first
options.body: Pause the PR until a bounded doctor or migration path establishes ownership for legacy rows.

recommendation.title: Approve strict ownership
recommendation.body: Keep fail-closed denial, document the non-plugin recovery path, and require deployed proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the projection seam and has the strongest history signal for persisted session storage behavior.
